question: How rapidly can the modeled state regenerate damaged local institutional capacity from centralized resources, relative to its own no-shock trajectory?
theory_role: State-side renewal/regeneration characterization. This is intentionally not called a state reproduction number because the current engine lacks endogenous state offspring creation.

design.focal_selection: even ranks across baseline local-institution capacity to span weak-to-strong structural contexts

shock: Multiply focal local institution capacity and administrative/legal/social/expected government-control dimensions by shock fraction. Preserve structural administrative capacity, geography, population, integrity, reach, and physical/fiscal control.
primary_estimand: Matched gap closure Q_S(t)=1-(C_control(t)-C_shock(t))/(C_control(0)-C_shock(0)), using shock_fraction=1 as the matched no-shock path at same seed/focal/capital multiplier.
predictions: Higher central capital weakly accelerates gap closure when government budget is resource-constrained.
Local structural capacity creates heterogeneous recovery rates even under equal central resources.
No-shock controls define the moving counterfactual and must not be treated as a fixed target.
falsifiers: Shocked paths do not systematically close gaps relative to no-shock controls.
Central resource variation has no effect even in demonstrably resource-constrained regimes.
Reported regeneration relies on foreign support or emergent insurgent dynamics.
promotion_guard: Synthetic characterization of implemented state regeneration only; not historical evidence and not a claim that real states share this functional form.
